features: A CREDIT NOTE NO LONGER CONSUMES BUDGET — Recording one, the simulation panel treated it as an expense: the chapter's remaining budget went down instead of up, and the cash panel showed an outflow that would never happen. On a € 61.00 credit note against a chapter with € 1,178.00 remaining, the remaining budget now rises to € 1,239.00 — not down — and cash stays unchanged, with «offsets, does not get cashed in» in place of a forecast outflow. This also applies to a chapter already over budget: previously, a credit note correcting it still triggered the overspend warning and demanded a justification for a document that frees up budget instead of consuming it.

THE WITHHOLDING ON A CREDIT NOTE BORN FROM A REVERSAL NO LONGER GETS LOST — When an invoice with withholding tax is reversed, the withheld amount is frozen onto the credit note it generates. If the supplier's record changed in the meantime — for example, moving to a flat-rate scheme — reopening that note even just to fix a date or a description recalculated the withholding from scratch, and saving left a balance owed to the Revenue Agency with no counterpart. The withholding now stays the one from the original, whatever changes in the supplier's record in the meantime — and the panel explaining it while editing no longer disappears along with everything else once the supplier becomes flat-rate, as it used to.

A CREDIT NOTE BORN FROM A REVERSAL CAN NO LONGER SHOW UP AS A PAYMENT TO OFFSET — This kind of note exists only to cancel an invoice, not to offset another one: a flaw in how it was tagged still left it offered in the automatic payment-offsetting panel. A verified case showed a real invoice marked «paid» against zero euros that actually left the cash account. The note is now excluded from every list of outstanding items and no longer appears among the possible actions on its row.

A REVERSED ROW IS NO LONGER STRUCK THROUGH — A document cancelled by a reversal showed its status and amount with a line through the text — a typographic mark meant for a price or a deleted word, not a coloured badge: on the invoice list it looked like a layout glitch more than a deliberate choice. The «Reversed» status and the amount now stay readable, just in a dimmed grey.

THE DOCUMENT TYPE IN EDIT MODE IS A LABEL, NOT A SELECTOR — While editing, the «Invoice / Credit note» button was still clickable even though it had no effect on saving — a document's type does not change by reopening it. It is now a single label with a lock icon, consistent with the other non-editable fields on the same page: to change a document's type, reverse it and record it again, as always.

ONE MORE CLARIFICATION ON «COUNTS TOWARD THE WITHHOLDING BASE» — The checkbox that decides whether a row's amount enters the withholding tax calculation now has a small question mark next to it, explaining when to leave it checked and when not to — useful when filling in an invoice by hand too, not only when reading it from an XML file.

THE WITHHOLDING PERCENTAGE NOW SHOWS UP EVERYWHERE IT APPLIES — The «Withholding» badge next to a supplier — both in the dropdown list and once selected — and the «Apply withholding tax» checkbox only said the supplier was subject to it, never at what rate: finding out meant opening their record. Both now show the percentage — «Withholding 4%», «Apply withholding tax 20%» — on all four pages where the badge appears (recording and editing an invoice, recording and editing a payment), and a question mark next to the checkbox explains what it does and when to uncheck it. Also fixed the «Counts toward the withholding base» checkbox's colour: like «Apply withholding tax» before this beta, it rendered blue instead of black from the same CSS class defect.
THE «INSUFFICIENT ACCOUNT BALANCE» DIALOG IS CLEARER — Its title used English-style capitalization on every word, and the «Cancel» button looked like plain text rather than a button. Both fixed.
